I live in Bay Ridge, Brooklyn, and it’s often underestimated when it comes to commuting. Few NYC neighborhoods have ferry, express bus, and subway access all in one place.
The NYC Ferry from the 69th Street Pier reaches Wall Street (Pier 11) in about 20 minutes, about 30 minutes to Battery Park City, and roughly 40 minutes to Midtown (East 39th Street). The X27 and X37 express buses can reach Downtown Manhattan in under 20 minutes depending on traffic and construction. The R train runs through the neighborhood, and the N express at nearby 59th Street can reach Times Square in about 30 minutes.
Bay Ridge also offers the Shore Road waterfront, Owl’s Head Park, great restaurants along Third and Fifth Avenue, good schools, and a strong community feel. It’s a quieter NYC neighborhood that still provides excellent access to Manhattan.

On the other hand, Oxford has grown a lot in the last 10-20 years and there is definitely some resentment among longtime residents. A lot of people are pretty invested in keeping Oxford 'rural' -- they don't like the new stores, they're suspicious of new people in town, etc. But for every person like that, we've met someone who is welcoming and kind. The way the town has rallied together since the record flooding has been inspiring.
